newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Banesto results due to prudent accounts.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Banesto results due to prudent accounts.

text.p: Banesto president Alfredo Saenz said on Thursday that the Spanish bank's 1996 accounts were conservative and prudent.
Banesto reported attributable profit of 26.04 billion pesetas, up 18.8 percent from 21.37 billion pta in 1995, lower than expected in a Reuter survey.
According to the Reuter survey, analysts had forecast on average attributable profit in Banesto at around 30.35 bln pta in 1996, in a range between 29 billion and 32.62 billion.
"We wanted to present conservative and prudent accounts," Saenz told reporters while presenting the bank's results.
He added that net attributable profit was below analysts' expectations because of provisions of about 8.7 billion pesetas for early retirements.
"We charged on 1996 accounts a fund of 8.67 billion pesetas to make provisions and pay funds to employees in early retirement," Saenz said.
This fund takes into account around three billion pesetas already paid for the previous year's payments. The remaing money is available for coming years' payments.
The 2.9 pct decline in net interest income stemmed from increased costs, such as to the deposit guarantee fund, or different accounting methods.
"In 1995 we had five billion pesetas from the money market operations which we didn't see this year, because we took this money into account as financial operations".
And then, Saenz added, the bank didn't have some extraordinary items that had the year before.
